title: Cappelletti Alpeggio
about: Antica Erboristeria Cappelletti, “the old herbalist’s,” was established in 1906 and for most of its first century worked from Piazza Fiera in the historic centre of Trento. Today the family firm sits in Aldeno, about 20 km south of the city, surrounded by vineyards and apple orchards. It is run by the fourth generation, Luigi and Maddalena Cappelletti, who still do all production in house, and it is best known for its red Aperitivo Cappelletti and a range of amari and aperitivi built on traditional herbs, roots and flowers.

An alpeggio is a high mountain pasture, and this liqueur sets out to bottle the smell of one in late summer. It draws on a hay-liqueur tradition shared across the Dolomites, the Austrian Alps and Bavaria. The wild grasses and flowers that make up mountain valley hay are cut, left to dry in the sun, then infused in neutral spirit and bottled at 24% alcohol. Cappelletti does not publish the individual plants in the blend.

It pours a deep amber with copper glints. The nose is grassy and floral, like dried meadow hay and green tea, and the palate is gently sweet, with honey, a little chocolate and a touch of cinnamon, finishing on green tea and caramel. The producer suggests sipping it neat or over ice just below room temperature, or lengthening it with soda or tonic; it also mixes with gin, rye or white rum, makes a fine digestif or hot toddy, and sits well beside alpine cheeses and cured meats.
facts: Sun-dried wild mountain hay – meadow grasses and flowers; individual plants not published
Neat or on ice at 15–18°C, or with soda or tonic
